title: Intermittent control-plane ejection and GPU-pool-drain chaos experiment to validate graceful degradation and SLO guardrails
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Validate that the platform gracefully degrades when (A) a single region's control plane experiences intermittent partitioning and request routing changes, and (B) a dominant GPU pool in another region is artificially drained/exhausted concurrently. We will also introduce a dependency blackhole for the metrics/feature-flag service to exercise fallback logic. This test verifies SLO preservation (latency P95 and error rate), correct circuit-breaker trips, load-shedding behavior, and automatic rollbacks/fallthroughs to lower-cost model variants or regional backups. Scope: Redwood hosted and Dedicated routing policies; do not run against customer private deployments without explicit customer consent. Hypothesis: Existing routing + fallback policies will keep end-to-end 95th percentile latency within SLO for non-burst traffic and will shed low-priority requests (non-interactive batch/async jobs) when GPU capacity drops below 30% in a region. Circuit-breakers should open for downstream blackholed dependencies within 15s and fall back to cached responses or error-failover paths. Metrics to collect: per-region p50/p95/p99 latency, per-endpoint error rate, GPU pool capacity/utilization, queue depth, number of circuit-breaker trips, load-shed counts, cost delta, and user-facing SLA alerts. Expected outcome: Documented list of gaps and an action plan: tuning load-shedding thresholds, improving circuit-breaker latency detection, and adjustments to routing weights for faster evacuation.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook executed without manual infra changes (all steps automated via chaos-control scripts)
End-to-end P95 latency for high-priority request class remains within SLO (<= 500ms) for >= 95% of test window
Error rate for high-priority class stays <= 1% for duration of test; low-priority class experiences controlled shedding with documented counts
Circuit breakers for blackholed dependency open within 15s and downstream fallbacks (cache or degraded feature) are used
Automated rollback triggers validated: system recovers to steady-state within 10 minutes after chaos is stopped
Observability dashboards capture all required signals and Grafana/Datadog alerts fire as expected
test_steps: 1) Prep: Deploy canary load generator in region-us-east and region-eu-west simulating mixed traffic classes (interactive, background batch). Ensure tokenized traces and KV cache warm-up are available.
2) Baseline: Collect 30m of steady-state metrics (latency histograms, GPU utilization, queue length, circuit-breaker metrics). Save snapshot to S3.

3) Inject A - Control-plane ejection: Using chaos-tool, create intermittent control-plane partition in us-east for 3 x 2-minute windows spaced 5 minutes apart. Simulate API router re-registration delays and routing table flaps.
4) Inject B - GPU pool drain: In eu-west, sequentially drain 70% of capacity from primary GPU pool over 10 minutes (simulate eviction/maintenance) forcing scheduling pressure and queueing.
5) Inject C - Dependency blackhole: For the duration of the middle 10 minutes, blackhole metrics/feature-flag service from runtime instances in both regions to force circuit-breaker detection.
6) Observe: Monitor circuit-breaker trips, fallback activations, model variant downgrades, and load-shedding counts. Record exact timestamps for each detected event.
7) Recovery: Disable chaos agents and bring capacity back. Verify automated rollback and traffic rebalancing completes within 10 minutes. Re-run baseline 30m to confirm steady-state.
8) Postmortem: Capture timeline, root causes, and improvement tasks. Create follow-ups for tuning thresholds and adding missing telemetry.
rollback_plan: If customer-impacting errors exceed acceptance thresholds or an unexpected region-wide outage occurs, abort test immediately via chaos-control kill-switch. Trigger global routing to fallback tier, enable canary rollback policy, and scale up dedicated emergency capacity (reserved pool) in unaffected regions. Pager duty: on-call SRE and service owner. Verify healthchecks and traces before resuming.
